name: Save All propagated frames eligibility
answer:
P0, OVERRIDING THE COMPLIANCE JUDGE, and both product questions answered.

PRIORITY FIRST. The panel split on whether this guards annotation data integrity. It decides which frames get exported and what class ids their objects carry, and the card records that it gets the class NAMES wrong: when a reference class has no alias, propagated frames export the label 'Class 3' while the reference frame exports '3' - so one propagation produces two different names for one class inside a single dataset. That is a corrupted export, not a cosmetic difference, and VOC and CreateML carry names rather than ids so there is no id to fall back on. P0.

SHOULD SAVE ALL FIRST COMMIT EDITS ON THE OPEN FRAME? Yes, and under decision 7 it asks rather than assuming. The alternative is what legacy does: Save All exports the STORED masks for every eligible frame, so a user who has just corrected the open frame and presses Save All exports the uncorrected version of it and their edit is gone. A bulk action must not silently discard the edit in front of it.

SHOULD OBJECTS WITH UNKNOWN CLASS BE SAVED AS CLASS 0? No. Class 0 is a real class a user can draw, so writing unknown objects into it silently merges them with a legitimate one and the result is indistinguishable afterwards. An object whose class cannot be resolved is a reportable condition: name the frames, say how many objects, and let the user assign a class or skip them. Refusing to guess is the same principle as everything else in decision 7.

AND THE ALIAS DEFECT IS FIXED RATHER THAN PRESERVED. A propagated object takes its reference object's class AND that class's alias, or no alias at all if there is none - never a manufactured 'Class N' string. 'Class N' is display text; it belongs in the UI and never in a file, which is the same rule RULE-042 states about the active-class marker.

The card also notes the confirmation message says NPZ when the save writes the selected formats. Ship the corrected wording.
